title: A CXL Memory Rack for Multi-Turn LLM Serving
event_hint: HyMCache: CXL-hybrid memory rack for multi-turn LLM KV-cache serving
problem: Multi-turn LLM serving requires TB-scale shared KV-cache capacity to reuse context across turns and sessions, but GPU HBM and host DRAM are too costly to scale to this level. Storage-backed tiers provide capacity but require software staging overhead. Pure DRAM-based CXL memory pools provide low latency but remain expensive at multi-TB scale.
mechanism: HyMCache builds a remote memory rack using CXL-hybrid memory (CXL-HM), which combines small in-device DRAM with large SSD-backed capacity behind a CXL.mem interface. It exploits read-dominant, predictable, and append-only KV-cache access patterns with request-level prefix prefetching and opportunistic write buffering to stage latency-critical reads in device DRAM, enabling DRAM-scale efficiency at SSD-level cost.

evidence.claim: CXL-HM prototype costs $10.5K-$11.0K vs Distributed Mooncake DRAM tier at $30K-$40K
evidence.baseline: Distributed Mooncake 1TB DDR5 RDIMM DRAM tier
evidence.condition: FPGA-based CXL-HM prototype with Agilex 7 development board, 64 GB device-side DRAM, two Gen5 SSDs; Mooncake uses 1 TB DDR5 RDIMM
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 10: Cost estimates for remote-tier components

evidence.claim: HyMCache hit ratio reaches 74% vs Distributed Mooncake at 65% in Qwen2.5-32B multi-turn serving
evidence.condition: 4P-1D-1S setup, Qwen2.5-32B model, mooncake trace workload, Turn 7
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 9, Figure 8: Hit ratio comparison

evidence.claim: Distributed Mooncake achieves ~30% higher performance than HyMCache but at 3-4x cost
evidence.condition: Qwen2.5-32B serving, same remote tier setup with ConnectX-6 RNIC and two Gen5 SSDs; Mooncake E2E TTFT 22.0s vs HyMCache 27.4s
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 10: Performance comparison and cost discussion

evidence.claim: HyMCache uses 16x less DRAM than 1TB distributed-DRAM Mooncake at ~30% performance gap
evidence.condition: HyMCache CXL-HM with 64 GB device-side DRAM; Mooncake with 1 TB DDR5 RDIMM; abstract claim - detailed metrics in evaluation section

evidence.claim: NVMe-oF raw bandwidth 23 GB/s per node but drops to 6.5 GB/s with XFS filesystem overhead
evidence.value: 23 GB/s raw vs 6.5 GB/s with XFS
evidence.condition: ConnectX-6 RNIC, 200 Gbps network limit, Gen5 SSDs, XFS-mounted NVMe-oF volume
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 10: Software I/O path overhead discussion

evaluation_context: Real CXL-HM prototype evaluation under two configurations: (1) single-aggregator serving, and (2) Prefill-Decode (PD) disaggregated serving with 64 GB per worker (256 GB total). Uses RDMA-capable network (ConnectX-6 RNIC, 100-200 Gbps) for remote memory access. Leverages vLLM serving engine with PagedAttention and Dynamo distributed framework with NIXL for P-D KV transfer. Models: Llama-3.1-8B (16 MB KV blocks) and Qwen2.5-32B (32 MB KV blocks) with FP16/BF16 KV cache and 128-token vLLM block size. Workloads: Dynamo AIPerf synthetic benchmark with mooncake trace, and LMSYS dataset for realistic multi-turn conversations. Setup: 4P-1D-1S (4 prefill, 1 decode, 1 scheduler) configuration.
limitations: Evidence pack covers abstract/intro/background and limited evaluation sections; some implementation details remain in unread sections. The 3.0x and 1.45x performance improvement claims from abstract are not directly validated in visible sections - concrete TTFT measurements show HyMCache at 27.4s vs LMCache at 17.2s for Qwen2.5-32B E2E median TTFT (Turn 1-7). Cost estimates are FPGA prototype projections, not production ASIC pricing. RDMA network RTT and queue depth characteristics are not explicitly measured. The supplement provides specific Mooncake comparison (22.0s vs 27.4s TTFT, ~30% performance gap) but does not validate the abstract multiplier claims. CXL-HM internal cache management policies are not detailed in visible text.
project_relevance: This source addresses KV-cache memory tiering for multi-turn LLM serving, which is highly relevant to cross-region cache sharing questions. The CXL-HM approach explores remote memory access over RDMA networks, which directly relates to WAN RTT and bandwidth considerations for KV cache transport. The 16x DRAM reduction versus 30% performance trade-off quantifies a key cost-performance decision point relevant to cross-region cache economics. Request-level prefix prefetching for predictable, append-only access patterns could inform compression and prefill strategies for cross-domain transfer. The measured NVMe-oF bandwidth degradation from 23 GB/s to 6.5 GB/s with filesystem overhead highlights software stack costs relevant to cross-domain transport. However, this paper focuses on intra-datacenter CXL/RDMA memory tiers rather than true WAN cross-region deployment; actual cross-region WAN latency (tens of ms) would be orders of magnitude higher than the CXL/RDMA latencies discussed. ConnectX-6 RNIC at 200 Gbps provides high-bandwidth intra-DC transport but does not represent WAN cross-region constraints.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the exact baseline LMCache configuration, workload characteristics (model, dataset, trace), and specific performance metrics (TTFT, TTFT, throughput, P99 latency) that support the 3.0x and 1.45x claims?
What are the actual RDMA network characteristics (RTT, bandwidth utilization, queue depths) and their impact on end-to-end serving latency?
